title: Boeing, Nvidia, CoreWeave, Newmont Lead Monday’s Biggest Stock Surges, CNBC Reports
body:
Shares of a diverse group of technology and mining firms surged on Monday, driven by a mix of corporate developments and market speculation. Nvidia’s board announced the return of co‑founder Jensen Huang to the chief executive chair, prompting a 20 % jump in CoreWeave, a cloud‑computing specialist that partners closely with the AI chipmaker, and a 12 % rise in Oracle’s stock. Meanwhile, Boeing’s shares fell sharply after the aerospace giant disclosed a larger‑than‑expected earnings shortfall, while New Mont’s gold‑mining stock rallied on higher spot prices and a positive production outlook. The moves, highlighted in a roundup of the day’s most active equities, underscore how quickly investor sentiment can pivot on leadership news, earnings surprises and commodity trends.

The most dramatic reaction came from CoreWeave, whose stock leapt 20 % after the company disclosed that Huang would re‑assume the Nvidia CEO role. CoreWeave, a fast‑growing provider of GPU‑intensive cloud services, has built its business on Nvidia’s hardware ecosystem. Market participants interpreted Huang’s return as a reaffirmation of Nvidia’s strategic focus on AI infrastructure, a narrative that directly benefits firms like CoreWeave that rely on Nvidia’s GPUs to power their services. Analysts at several boutique firms upgraded CoreWeave to a “buy” rating, citing the firm’s expanding customer base and the expected surge in demand for AI‑driven workloads. The rally also lifted other “neocloud” players, including Nebius and IREN, which saw modest gains as investors broadened their bets on the emerging cloud‑AI niche.

Oracle’s 12 % surge was similarly linked to the Nvidia leadership news, albeit through a different channel. The software giant has been positioning itself as a cloud provider for AI workloads, and its recent partnership with Nvidia to integrate the latter’s GPUs into Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) has been a cornerstone of that strategy. With Huang back at the helm, investors anticipate accelerated development of AI‑centric services and a deeper integration of Nvidia technology across Oracle’s platform. The stock’s ascent was further bolstered by a better‑than‑expected earnings beat, which reinforced confidence in the company’s ability to monetize its AI initiatives.

In stark contrast, Boeing’s shares tumbled more than 8 % after the company released quarterly results that fell short of Wall Street forecasts. The aerospace manufacturer cited lingering supply‑chain bottlenecks, a slowdown in commercial aircraft orders, and higher warranty costs as primary drivers of the miss. While defense contracts remain robust, the broader market remains wary of Boeing’s ability to meet its production targets for the 737 MAX and 777X families. Credit rating agencies downgraded the firm’s outlook, citing elevated debt levels and the need for sustained cash flow to fund ongoing development programs. Analysts warned that any further delays could exacerbate the stock’s downward pressure, especially as airlines continue to grapple with fluctuating fuel prices and demand uncertainties.

Gold miner New Mont also made headlines, with its shares climbing roughly 5 % after the company reported higher-than‑expected gold output and benefited from a rally in spot gold prices, which have risen above $2,200 an ounce. The firm’s management highlighted successful exploration projects in Nevada and a disciplined cost‑control strategy that helped improve margins despite a volatile commodity environment. Investors view New Mont as a relatively low‑risk play in the precious‑metals sector, given its strong balance sheet and diversified asset base. The rally was part of a broader uptick in mining stocks, reflecting investor appetite for safe‑haven assets amid lingering geopolitical tensions and inflation concerns.

Overall, Monday’s market activity illustrated how leadership changes at a marquee tech firm can ripple through adjacent industries, while earnings disappointments and commodity price movements continue to exert decisive influence on stock trajectories. As the week progresses, market participants will be watching closely for further guidance from Nvidia’s new‑old CEO, as well as any updates from Boeing’s production schedule and the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy stance. The interplay of these factors is likely to shape investor sentiment across both the technology and commodities arenas in the coming days.
